edges.how: For the square three-by-three member in this constructor's orientation, promote all horizontal ZZ gauge pairs to stabilizers. Together with the two X center generators, they reproduce the repository's nine-qubit Shor stabilizer row space exactly; the discarded gauge freedom becomes fixed. The neighboring Shor entry uses encoded-basis names that call the Z column logical X and the X row logical Z, so its logical labels are swapped relative to this card's Pauli-type names even though the protected Pauli algebra is the same.

Plain rectangular Bacon–Shor occupies every site of the defining binary matrix. Bravyi–Bacon–Shor permits a general occupancy matrix and derives encoded dimension and distances from its row and column codes, so its rate claims do not transfer to the full rectangle.

Promoting selected gauge generators to commuting stabilizers produces two-dimensional compass-code descendants between the Bacon–Shor and surface-like extremes. The pattern of promoted checks is part of the target code and is not encoded by changing only rows and columns here.

The protected X and Z parities are perpendicular repetition constraints, with local pair checks liberated into a gauge subsystem. This quotient is the subsystem analogue of Shor's nested repetition construction rather than an HGP replay recipe.
Bivariate bicycle codes are the abelian two-block group-algebra codes for Z_l x Z_m; general 2BGA codes may use other groups and need not have a two-variable polynomial presentation.

This entry fixes the 4.8.8 bulk tiling and one explicit triangular three-color boundary convention inside the wider family of two- dimensional color codes on trivalent, face-three-colorable cellulations. The parent target is pending as a separate Atlas entry.

The 4.8.8 and 6.6.6 tilings realize the same two-dimensional color-code order, while their face weights, finite boundary staircases, qubit counts, extraction circuits, and decoder graphs remain different.

Local Clifford unfolding produces surface-code sectors on derived lattices. With boundaries those sectors can remain attached along a fold, so this relation is a representation map rather than the direct constructor recipe for the shipped incidence matrices.
This entry fixes the honeycomb bulk tiling and one explicit triangular three-color boundary convention inside the wider family of 2D color codes on trivalent, face-three-colorable cellulations.

Local Clifford unfolding maps a closed 2D color code to two surface-code copies; for the triangular boundary, the copies remain attached along a fold. This is an equivalence dictionary, not the constructor recipe used for the exact face-incidence matrix here.

The 6.6.6 and 4.8.8 tilings realize the same abstract 2D color-code order, while face weights, finite-boundary staircases, qubit counts, and extraction circuits differ and must not be transferred numerically.

The protocol begins and returns to an effective two-dimensional color code, but uses an ordered low-weight measurement path through different instantaneous frames. The relation targets the broader static family; it does not identify this schedule with the existing 6.6.6 or 4.8.8 finite-boundary entries.
This entry fixes the two-dimensional color substrate, Pauli-triangle boundary, and phi_(rbg) schedule inside the wider construction class of measurement paths that realize topological automorphisms.

The reference frame has color-code topological order, while its doubled microscopic qubits, Pauli boundaries, docking sites, and time-dependent checks differ from the static three-color-boundary 6.6.6 constructor. Bulk phase does not transfer finite parameters or decoder results.

The no-error alternative and all single-qubit Pauli faults occupy every four-bit syndrome exactly once. This identifies one perfect block; it does not equate the entry with the full quantum-perfect class.

The verified parameters saturate the quantum Singleton equality. The edge records class membership while the entry remains the binary cyclic representative rather than the family of all quantum MDS codes.
The cyclic stabilizer is one explicit Frobenius-code example in the Dutta-Kurur construction. Other Frobenius lengths and alphabets are not aliases of this fixed block.

The global-X/global-Z [[k+2,k,2]] Iceberg construction reduces at its smallest nontrivial size to this exact stabilizer block. The relation identifies a family specialization; it does not replace the present entry by the whole variable-size family.

The canonical entry fixes the qubit CSS polynomial pair 1+x+y+z and 1+xy+yz+zx. Generalized Haah codes alter the local polynomial data or coefficient field; they contain this choice as a specialization but are not aliases of every periodic Code 1 instance. The target entry is pending.

Ungauging the cubic code produces a spin model with fractal subsystem symmetries, while gauging reverses the dictionary under the assumptions of the construction. This is a representation-changing duality, not a finite-depth logical gate on the same periodic Hilbert space. The target entry is pending.

After each round, contracting the just-measured matching and applying a depth-one local Clifford change of basis maps the instantaneous stabilizer group to toric-code stabilizers on a coarser lattice. The equivalence is frame-by-frame; the full protocol still has spacetime detectors and a nontrivial anyon automorphism.

The family fixes the symmetric HGP specialization HGP(H,H) and then restricts H to biregular Tanner factors satisfying two-sided small-set expansion. The constructor regression compares every exported CSS row literally with qeclib.constructions.hgp; generic HGP codes need not meet the expansion hypotheses and are not aliases of this family.

This fixed block is the four-coordinate member of the binary CSS quantum Hamming construction. The relation records that family specialization without replacing this EC-Zoo-mapped fixed-block identity by the variable-length family.

In the shared ordering of the fifteen nonzero four-bit labels, retain the four Hamming X checks and enlarge the four-dimensional Hamming Z row space to the ten-dimensional orthogonal complement of the coordinate rows plus the all-one row. The six added commuting Z constraints fix six Hamming logical degrees of freedom, changing k from seven to one. The entry regression verifies both row-space containment and the target constructor, so the two blocks are related by gauge-out rather than identified as alternative presentations.
Syndrome-conditioned gauge fixing moves a logical state between the Steane block, where Clifford operations are transversal, and this block, where the non-Clifford phase is transversal.
This fixed block is the punctured four-variable member obtained from binary Reed–Muller evaluation spaces; the target family entry is not yet present, so the relation intentionally remains pending.

The punctured evaluation construction has a tetrahedral 3D color-code realization. The geometry and Boolean table describe the same encoded block, while larger 3D color codes are not generated by simply enlarging this tetrahedron.

Code deformation can split a suitable surface-code patch into two repetition blocks and later use their shared layout for joint parity processing. The finite boundary geometry, syndrome rounds, and decoder are part of the switch; an isolated chain is not identical to a surface code.

Three length-three bit-flip repetition blocks are the physical symbols of a length-three phase-flip repetition code. At matrix level, H_Z is three block-diagonal copies of the open repetition parity matrix and H_X is the outer parity matrix expanded across complete inner blocks. This is a curated construction relation: the repository has no exact concatenation replay adapter, so this card deliberately omits a construction recipe instead of presenting the relation as verifier evidence.
The three paired weight-four faces form the smallest triangular 6.6.6 color-code patch; larger triangular patches belong to the color-code family rather than a size parameter of this fixed block.
Fault-tolerant conversion trades Steane's transversal Clifford set for the fifteen-qubit Reed-Muller block's transversal non-Clifford gate, then converts back.
HGP(rep_L, rep_L) — the planar surface code is the hypergraph product of two repetition codes
The same square-lattice star/plaquette bulk is obtained from HGP(rep_L, rep_L); open repetition factors give the planar Surface patch, while periodic factors close it into the toric code.

HGP(C_L, C_L^T), where C_L is the square cyclic neighbor-parity map, reproduces the ordered Toric check matrices exactly. These periodic square factors are not the open rep_L factors used by the planar Surface construction recipe.

Both use the square-lattice star and plaquette bulk. Cutting the torus creates rough and smooth boundaries and changes absolute cycles into relative strings; closing those boundaries restores two periodic homology directions. Bulk equivalence is not code-space identity.

At the appropriate frames, contracting the just-measured Honeycomb matching and applying a depth-one local Clifford basis change gives Toric stabilizers on a coarser lattice. The full Honeycomb object remains a time-periodic measurement protocol with spacetime detectors and an anyon automorphism.

Binary HGP is the length-two CSS specialization of the broader homological-product operation on chain complexes. Surface and quantum-expander entries instead point to this construction with typed product_of edges; reversing those edges would confuse an operation with one of its output families.
